input: Draft a short script for a YouTube explainer video

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The topic entirely determines the content, structure, and depth of the script — without it, nothing can be written.
Knowing the target audience (age, expertise level, background) shapes vocabulary, analogies, and how much to explain.
The intended video length dictates how many words to write and how much detail to include — a 2-min script is very different from a 10-min one.
The channel's niche or existing style (educational, entertainment, corporate, personal brand) affects tone and framing of the script.
Tone and style choices — serious vs. casual, humorous vs. neutral — fundamentally change how the script reads and feels.
Knowing the primary goal (drive subscribers, explain a product, teach a concept, promote a service) determines what the script must achieve by the end.
Whether the script needs a voiceover-only format, on-camera presenter cues, or visual/B-roll directions changes how it is structured and formatted.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a YouTube explainer video script
gold.taskDescription: Write a short script for a YouTube explainer video on an unspecified topic, for an unspecified audience and channel.

questions.title: What specific topic should the video explain?
questions.description: Identify the exact subject or concept the explainer video is about, so the script content can be written.

questions.title: Who is the intended audience for this video?
questions.description: Clarify the target viewer — their age range, familiarity with the topic, and general background — to calibrate language and depth.

questions.title: How long should the finished video be?
questions.description: Establish the target runtime (e.g. 2, 5, or 10 minutes) so the script can be sized appropriately in word count and detail.

questions.title: What kind of channel or brand is this video for?
questions.description: Understand the channel's niche, identity, or industry context so the script fits its existing style and framing.

questions.title: What tone should the script have — casual, formal, or humorous?
questions.description: Pin down the desired voice and energy of the script so it matches how the creator wants to come across to viewers.

questions.title: What should viewers do or feel by the video's end?
questions.description: Define the primary goal — e.g. understand a concept, buy a product, subscribe, change a behaviour — so the script has a clear payoff and call to action.

questions.title: Should the script include on-screen visual or presenter cues?
questions.description: Determine the format needed — plain voiceover prose, on-camera speaker directions, or B-roll and graphic callouts — so the script is structured correctly.
